items.evidence: The first section after the title is "## The bottom line", whose three bold heads run in the required order: "**1. What FRUS answers directly.**" (line 5), "**2. Where FRUS points for the rest.**" (line 7), "**3. What this request cannot get from FRUS.**" (line 21). A "**Scope.**" paragraph and "## Decisions this needs from you" follow, and "## Findings" begins only at line 38, after all three parts.

The file holds no percent sign and no bare figure. Every number is a count of a named set or a rate of one: "about 1,900 of the 2,300 documents carry one"; "about one time in four for 1913–1929, against about one time in ten before 1913" in "the editors' recognition chapters"; "only 23 of the 40 were about recognizing a government"; "all but two of the 384 documents dated through 1905 carry none"; "the control search found 67 and 337 documents in the two volumes, and the impossible string none". The closest calls still carry their base: the library list elides the unit after its first item ("15 documents; ... 6; ... 2" and "(9)", "(8)", all documents from the named collection), and "within a factor of two of their rates across the whole series" is a ratio against a named baseline, not a bare percentage.

Forty-five history.state.gov links resolve to 41 distinct documents, the "41 documents" the collection holds, and every one is cited in full each time it appears, never shortened to a document number alone: "(Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, 1877, Document 222, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1877/d222)"; "(Papers Relating to the Foreign Relations of the United States, The Lansing Papers, 1914–1920, Volume II, Document 384, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1914-20v02/d384)"; "(Foreign Relations of the United States, 1964–1968, Volume XXXI, South and Central America; Mexico, Document 141, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1964-68v31/d141)". Volumes with no part or volume number (1900, 1913, 1917) are cited as the printed edition prints them. No citation is a bare id pair or a title alone.

The absences that rest on a zero are each a search with terms, volumes and controls: "I searched every chapter and section heading in all 553 volumes for the words recognition, revolution, coup, junta, de facto, provisional government, overthrow and insurrection. From 1950 on, only one Latin American heading names recognition ... a separate search found eight documents (a control search for the phrase Department of State found 27 in the same pages, and an impossible string found none)"; for the 1980s, the two volumes are named and "the control search found 67 and 337 documents in the two volumes, and the impossible string none"; the question's own words "appear in two, 25 and 32 of the roughly 1,200 documents in the editors' recognition chapters, within a factor of two of their rates across the whole series"; the nineteenth-century files rest on a count, "all but two of the 384 documents dated through 1905 carry none". One of the five bullets is an assertion with no search behind it: "FRUS prints what the new governments told American diplomats ... but not their own deliberations. Nothing in the bundled data points to those archives." It claims no zero from a search, so the section as a whole is stated by measurement; a reader who wants every bullet measured should weigh that bullet.

A scan of the file found no SQL keyword, no table or column name, no file path and no percent sign. Every volume/document id occurs only as the path of a required history.state.gov link ("https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1948v09/d7"), never as a bare string in prose. The data are described in words: "a read-only copy of the FRUS Explorer index covering all 553 volumes", "the bundled lot index", "the separate citation index". The decimal file numbers ("8xx.00", "817.00") and filing codes ("POL 16") are the National Archives' and the Department's own designations, not database names.

judge:r2.rankingReason:
r2: passes all five tests cleanly; states the test and the asks most directly (two bookend statements, three departures, the asks by period), quantifies the consequence of every definitional decision, measures its own precision (23 of 40), keeps every citation complete, and its collection carries a note per document and a threads-not-followed close.
r7: the widest evidence (58 documents, 1865–1980, per-decade rates, the literal re-test of its set, three editors' sentences set aside) and the best measured shape of the record; but citations drop to short form after a volume's first mention, one "cannot get" search names no terms ("a coup-policy phrase"), and the findings are walls of quotation.
r6: 43 documents with the fullest archival pointers (entry, identifier, dates, access status for each lot) and a Part 3 whose every absence names its terms and both controls; the quote bullets carry no links and prose citations shorten after the first.
r5: 56 documents, every citation complete, the plainest prose, honest that 1861–1876 and post-1980 went unsearched; but few measured rates, its main Part 3 search defers the volume list to the memo and keeps its controls in the method section, and the decimal file's dates are muddled ("1910 to 1949").
r9: a vivid narrative with extents and access status and a measured 1861–1875 residue; but its Part 3 says the inter-American resolutions appear only in editors' footnotes while r2 and r4 quote their operative text from documents, and its Tobar count (eighty-eight documents) almost certainly counts a surname that r4 found names the doctrine once.
r4: careful measurement (strict and loose phrase forms, term against corpus baseline, controls on all 74 volumes) but only 19 documents in five findings, too thin a base for the historian.
r3: 38 documents offered as "a selection of the best evidence, not a census", citations by sender, recipient and date without the document number, an Afghanistan document among the Latin American findings, a briefing read only in part, and a long list of cases it found but did not read.

items.evidence: queries.log line 1 is `sqlite3 "file:...?mode=ro" "SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT volume_id), COUNT(*), SUM(is_front_matter), SUM(is_editorial_note) FROM document_cache;"`; memo [M-COV]: "returned `553|321749|1103|8481`, as required: 553 volumes, 321,749 documents, 1,103 front-matter rows, 8,481 editorial notes." I re-ran it against the copy and got the same row.

Memo [M-COV]: "Every count in this memo is conditional on these 553 volumes (the full series as the manifest lists it)." Overview, Scope: "Every count here is conditional on the 553 volumes in this copy of the index, which is the whole series as the app lists it." Collection intro: "137 of the 553 volumes in this copy of the index".

Memo cites every document as the pair, e.g. [M-ANCH] "frus1913/d7 ... frus1913/d1028, frus1914/d544, frus1914/d568, frus1943v05/d33, frus1943v05/d142, frus1964-68v31/d206" and §6 "Q1 — frus1900/d530 (offset 1439 of 3792 characters...)"; the collection's 41 document entries each carry `volumeId` and `documentId`.

`grep -rn -i rowid` over memo.md, overview.md, queries.log, collection.fruscollection, scripts/ and out/sql_trace.log returns nothing; every identifier in the memo, trace and collection is a (volume_id, document_id) pair.

All six distinct JOIN clauses in out/sql_trace.log use both keys, e.g. "JOIN document_cache c ON c.volume_id = f.volume_id AND c.document_id = f.document_id LEFT JOIN document_dates d ON d.volume_id = f.volume_id AND d.document_id = f.document_id"; the VALUES-list joins read "JOIN s ON ds.volume_id = s.v AND ds.document_id = s.d" ([M-CF], [M-PA]); Python-side sets and dicts are keyed on tuples, e.g. rule_recall.py `C = {(r["volume_id"], r["document_id"]) ...}`, decades.py `meta = {(v, d): ...}`. No single-key join found.

Memo [M-RULE]: "SCOPE = C ∪ T, apparatus excluded (`is_front_matter = 0 AND is_editorial_note = 0`)"; [M-T]: "The MATCH returns 3,496 documents corpus-wide (66 of them apparatus); 1,358 sit in Latin American sections; 1,348 of those are not apparatus = T"; [M-C] "3 are apparatus; C = 1,206"; the decade, false-friend and absence SQL all carry `c.is_front_matter = 0 AND c.is_editorial_note = 0`. My check of the collection's 41 pairs found no front-matter or editorial-note row.

The reading SELECT in out/sql_trace.log (52 read_docs.py lines) selects "c.document_number, c.header, c.dateline, c.source_note, c.body_text, length(c.body_text), c.is_front_matter, c.is_editorial_note, d.date_iso" and nothing else; `grep -c -i "summary_text|note_text"` over out/sql_trace.log and every script's SQL is 0 (the only mentions are the memo's [M-QUOTED] sentence and a comment in read_docs.py saying they were never selected). All 26 quotations are substrings of body_text.

The cross_references table was never used: `grep -rn -i cross_ref` over memo.md, overview.md, queries.log, scripts/ and out/sql_trace.log returns nothing; the only pointed-at channel used is external_citations ([M-PA]).

score:r2.notes: All four files were present (memo.md 427 lines, overview.md, collection.fruscollection, queries.log), plus scripts/, out/, raw/ and quotes/ in the run directory. Independent verification against the read-only copy, the TEI volumes' census outputs and the bundled JSON reproduced every figure tested: the canary row 553|321749|1103|8481; the T MATCH 3,496 and the stem-trap variant 2,975 (and the mechanism: vocab holds `provision` = stem of 'provisional' beside `provis` = stem of 'provision'); out/ff_sql_on.sql -> 1206|638|25|2|32|260|123|137; out/arch_sql_document_sources.sql -> 1,929 rows on 1,929 documents; the decade denominators 11268/5821/6484/9845/10261/30842/20374/40073/75872/43159/27654/22640/6038; the TEI census cells on disk (CONSTITUTIONAL 13/128 and 91/341, CA_TREATY 66/321, CONSULT_FORMAL 36/416, AXIS 65/416, COMMUNISM 174/292, HUMAN_RIGHTS 25/292); all 26 quotations as exact substrings of body_text; the collection's 41 distinct pairs (none apparatus, none Ed2, all 23 excerpts exact substrings); lot 62D1 -> NAID 2838992 with status 'Restricted - Partly' and creator 'Policy Planning Council'; RG 59 -> NAID 388; all 61 trace-table anchors at the stated memo lines. E3 is not_applicable because cross_references was never used. Residues an adjudicator may weigh: (1) P6: headings_dump.py's single SELECT is missing from out/sql_trace.log while the memo's intro and §9 describe that file as holding every statement a script ran; the statement is shown in queries.log line 9 and [M-HEAD], and queries.log itself declares its elisions, so scored obeyed. (2) O1: volume/document ids appear only inside history.state.gov canonical URLs within full edition citations; scored obeyed as a reader-facing link, not a bare id pair. (3) S5: the Ed2 check covers the scope and collection; the corpus-wide denominators (decade corpus column, false-friend ALL 312,169) include the three Ed2 volumes unfolded without a statement, immaterial to the factor-of-two reading.
